# Your mutual funds are on Zerodha and Groww. Can one loan cover both?


*By Ashutosh Purohit*


If you've been investing for a few years, your mutual funds are probably scattered. There's the SIP you started on Groww, the index funds you later bought on Zerodha Coin, and maybe an old folio with CAMS from when you invested through your bank. Then you need money, you don't want to sell, and the first question is whether one loan can cover all of it.


It can. You just need a lender that accepts both ways your funds can be held.


There are two of them. A mutual fund is held either in a **demat account** , the same place your shares sit, or as a **statement of account (SOA)** directly with the fund's registrar, CAMS or KFintech. (Wondering why there are two? We explain where each came from in[demat vs SOA: the two ways to hold mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/blog/demat-vs-soa-mutual-funds) .) For borrowing, what matters is that not every lender accepts both for a pledge.


Yenmo does. Your Zerodha and Groww holdings, your CAMS and KFintech funds and any shares you own go into one loan account with one limit. Loans start at ₹25,000, the lender is Bajaj Finance, and there's no annual fee and no foreclosure charge.


**The short version**


- What matters is how your funds are held, demat or SOA, not the app you bought them on.
- Many lenders handle only one form. Yenmo handles both, plus shares, in a single account.
- You don't need to move or convert anything before you borrow.
- You pay interest only on what you withdraw, with no annual fee for the full 3 years.


## Why don't all lenders accept both?


Your funds aren't really "in" Zerodha or Groww. The app is just where you bought them. Zerodha Coin keeps mutual funds in demat. Groww can hold them either way. Funds bought straight from a fund house or through a distributor are usually SOA.


The catch is that each form is pledged through a different system. For SOA units, the lender asks CAMS or KFintech to mark a lien, which is a hold that stops you redeeming those units while the loan is open. For demat units, it creates a pledge through the depository, the same way shares are pledged.


Plenty of lenders have built only one of these routes. A broker's own loan product is usually built around holdings in its own demat account. That's why most answers online end with "find a lender that accepts both" and stop there.


## How do I know which form my funds are in?


Open your broker's holdings. If a fund shows up in your demat holdings, it's in demat. If it has a folio number and appears on a CAMS or KFintech statement but not in your demat account, it's SOA. A Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) shows both in one place.


You don't have to work this out before applying to Yenmo, because we take both. It just helps to know, since the two are pledged differently.


SOA (statement of account) Demat


Recorded with CAMS or KFintech A depository (CDSL or NSDL), through your broker


Usually bought through A fund house, a distributor, or Groww Zerodha Coin, other brokers, and some Groww accounts


How it's pledged Lien marked with the registrar Pledge through the depository


Can shares go in the same pledge? No Yes


## What are your options?


There are four ways to deal with funds spread across apps, and only one of them saves you work.


You could borrow from your broker's lending arm. That's easy if everything is in that broker's demat account, but funds held anywhere else usually won't count.


You could convert everything into one form first. Converting between SOA and demat doesn't sell your units, but it means forms and waiting. Fine if you're not in a hurry.


You could take two loans. It works, but now you have two limits, two sets of fees and two interest bills to keep track of.


Or you could use a lender that accepts both forms. One application, one account, one limit. That's how Yenmo is built.


## How does it work on Yenmo?


Yenmo is a loan service provider. We run the app and handle your application, and the loan itself comes from our RBI-regulated lending partner, Bajaj Finance. Because we aren't a broker, we're not tied to any one demat account.


The application itself takes 5–7 minutes:


1. Check your eligibility at[lamf.yenmo.in](https://lamf.yenmo.in/) with the mobile number linked to your investments.
2. Pledge your SOA holdings with CAMS and KFintech through our digital flow.
3. Add your demat funds and shares from Zerodha, Groww, Upstox or any other broker. More than one demat account is fine; add them all. For now this step starts with an email tosupport@yenmo.in , and after that it's fully digital, with no forms. We're working on making it completely self-serve.
4. Complete KYC with your PAN, Aadhaar and bank account.
5. Withdraw what you need, as little as ₹500 at a time, up to your limit.


Everything lands in one loan account. Your limit, and the interest rate it qualifies for, are based on the combined value of everything you've pledged. You approve each pledge yourself, and nothing is sold.


The question we hear most from people with funds in more than one place is simple: why isn't my fund showing up? Almost always, it's held in the other form. Once we explain the two ways funds are held, it clicks.


The next question is whether their funds move to us. They don't. The units stay in your name, and the only thing that changes is that a lien is marked on them. It's lifted when you repay.


People also ask whether they'll have to contact us again to get their funds released. You won't. In the Yenmo app or on our website, pick the fund and the number of units you want to unpledge, and press a button.


Unpledging has to be done by the lender, so we send your request to Bajaj Finance directly through our systems. There's no form to fill in and no email to write. If you still owe money, the funds that stay pledged need to cover it;[here's how unpledging works while a loan is active](https://yenmo.in/blog/can-you-unpledge-mutual-funds-while-loan-is-active) .


## How much could you borrow? An example


Say you have:


- ₹3 lakh in equity index funds on Zerodha Coin (demat)
- ₹2 lakh in equity funds bought on Groww, held as SOA with CAMS
- ₹1 lakh in a liquid fund, held with KFintech


Through Yenmo, Bajaj Finance lends up to 50% of the value of equity funds and up to 90% of liquid funds. So your equity funds support ₹2.5 lakh (half of ₹5 lakh) and your liquid fund supports ₹90,000. That's a limit of up to ₹3.4 lakh, all in one account.


A ₹3.4 lakh limit falls in the ₹2 lakh–₹10 lakh slab, so your rate is 10.39% a year. Now say you withdraw ₹2 lakh. You pay interest on ₹2 lakh, not ₹3.4 lakh: about ₹1,732 a month. There's no EMI, and you can repay the principal whenever you like within the 3 years, at no extra charge.


This assumes all your funds are on the lender's approved list, since only approved funds count. To try your own numbers, use the[loan against mutual funds calculator](https://yenmo.in/calculators/loan-against-mutual-fund-calculator) .

You'll see 11% on our charges page too. That's the maximum Bajaj Finance's loan terms allow, and we're required to show it. No loan through Yenmo is priced above 10.49% today.


Beyond interest, there's a one-time processing fee of ₹1,649 + GST, which covers stamp duty and your first pledge and unpledge. There's no annual or renewal fee for the 3-year term; we guarantee that on every Bajaj Finance loan through Yenmo. Paying early, in part or in full, costs nothing.


You don't need a minimum credit score. Pledge, unpledge and depository charges are on the[charges page](https://yenmo.in/charges) , and the product itself is explained on the[loan against mutual funds](https://yenmo.in/products/loan-against-mutual-funds) page.


## What should you know before pledging?


A few things catch people out.


Not every fund counts. Lenders accept only funds on their approved list, and ELSS units still in their lock-in can't be pledged.


Pledged units stay invested in your name, but you can't redeem or switch them until they're unpledged. If you might need a particular fund soon, leave it out. More on this in[whether you can unpledge while a loan is active](https://yenmo.in/blog/can-you-unpledge-mutual-funds-while-loan-is-active) .


If markets fall, your limit falls with them. If you've withdrawn more than the new limit, the lender can ask you to repay part of it or pledge more units. Borrowing well below your limit gives you a cushion.


Bajaj Finance lends to borrowers aged 21 to 70.


## What do the RBI rules allow?


RBI sets the ceiling, and each lender can stay below it. NBFCs such as Bajaj Finance can lend up to 50% of the value of equity mutual funds, under the[NBFC Credit Facilities Directions, 2025](https://rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12957) . Since 1 July 2026, banks can lend up to 75% against equity funds and 85% against debt funds, capped at ₹1 crore per person against shares and equity funds ([RBI/2025-26/254](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13346&Mode=0) ).


## Getting started


You don't have to tidy up your portfolio before you borrow. Check your eligibility at[lamf.yenmo.in](https://lamf.yenmo.in/) with the mobile number linked to your investments, and if you have funds or shares in demat, write tosupport@yenmo.in and we'll take it from there. If you also hold shares, here's how[stocks and mutual funds work together in one account](https://yenmo.in/blog/borrow-against-stocks-and-mutual-funds-in-one-account) .


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I take one loan against mutual funds held on both Zerodha and Groww?


Yes, if the lender accepts both demat units and SOA holdings with CAMS or KFintech. Zerodha keeps mutual funds in demat, while Groww holdings can be in either form. On Yenmo, both forms, plus shares, go into one account, so you don't need to move anything to one broker first.


### Can I get a loan against mutual funds held in demat form versus statement form, and does the process differ?


You can borrow against both, but they're pledged differently. SOA units get a lien marked with the registrar, CAMS or KFintech. Demat units are pledged through the depository, the same way as shares. On Yenmo the two go through separate steps but end up in the same loan account.


### Can I pledge mutual funds in Groww?


Yes. Funds bought on Groww can be pledged whether they're held in demat or as SOA with CAMS or KFintech. Yenmo accepts both, with loans from ₹25,000.


### How do I pledge mutual funds held in Zerodha?


Funds on Zerodha Coin sit in your demat account, so they're pledged through the depository, like shares. On Yenmo you add them through the demat step, which for now starts with an email tosupport@yenmo.in , and they join the same account as any SOA holdings with CAMS or KFintech. The loan is from Bajaj Finance.


### Do I need to move my mutual funds to one broker before taking a loan?


Not on Yenmo. Demat holdings with Zerodha, Groww, Upstox or other brokers, and SOA holdings with CAMS or KFintech, all go into one account. You'd only need to move or convert units if your lender accepts just one form or one broker's demat account.


### How much loan can I get against my mutual fund portfolio?


Through Yenmo, Bajaj Finance lends up to 50% of the value of equity funds, up to 90% of liquid funds and typically 70%–80% of other debt funds. Loans start at ₹25,000 and go up to ₹5 crore online. RBI allows NBFCs up to 50% on equity funds and banks up to 75%.
